name: Split-screen demo
summary: Screen recording on top, you on the bottom, captions on the seam. For showing a tool, a process or a result.
bestFor: Walking through a tool, a dashboard or a before/after
Proof content: show the real screen while you explain it
Anything where the viewer needs to see what you are talking about
needs: One or more screen recordings (or screenshots) of what you talk about

modes.use: The hook (first 2 to 3 s) and the call to action: face only.
Most of the video: the visual on top, you underneath.
Every 10 to 15 s for 2 to 4 s when a detail on screen needs the whole frame.

overlaySlots.when: The hook, frame 1 to about 2.5 s.
When a line cites a page, a result or a source: show it with a source chip.
When a line states a number that changed (before/after).

notes: Change the top visual every 3 to 6 s so the screen never sits still.
Line the visual change up with the sentence that mentions it.
A soft whoosh on layout changes only; never on a cut inside a sentence.
Screen recordings come first; stills only for sources and results.

evidence.choice: Show the screen while you talk
evidence.why: Seeing the real tool or result is proof; it beats describing it and keeps attention on the claim.
A static top half reads as a screenshot and gets skipped; regular changes hold attention.
Between the two halves they cover neither your face nor the screen detail.

evidence.choice: Every number on screen backed by evidence
evidence.why: A number the viewer can check builds trust; an unbacked one costs it.
